title: Book of Kells & Trinity Long Room
description: One of the world's most famous illuminated manuscripts, housed in the architecturally stunning Long Room at Trinity College. The library itself is as jaw-dropping as the book — 200,000 ancient texts lining a barrel-vaulted chamber that inspired Star Wars and Harry Potter.
availabilityNote: Book online — sells out, especially weekends

title: MoLI — Museum of Literature Ireland
description: A beautiful museum dedicated to Irish writing in a Georgian building on St Stephen's Green. Extraordinary first editions, handwritten manuscripts, and a sensory recreation of Leopold Bloom's bedroom. One of Dublin's most underrated cultural experiences.

title: Photo Museum Ireland
description: The best photography exhibition space in Ireland, tucked into Temple Bar. Rotating shows from Irish and international photographers alongside the finest collection of photography books in the country. Free, thoughtful, and consistently surprising.
availabilityNote: Free entry — check current exhibition before going

title: Winding Stair Bookshop
description: A beloved independent bookshop on the banks of the Liffey near the Ha'penny Bridge, with shelves crammed with carefully chosen Irish and international titles. Upstairs is an award-winning restaurant with views over the river — easy to turn a browse into an afternoon.

title: Gutter Bookshop
description: A proper Dublin institution in Temple Bar, named after the Oscar Wilde quote. Independently owned, passionately curated, and always good for a recommendation. One of those bookshops you walk into for ten minutes and leave an hour later.

title: Books Upstairs
description: One of Dublin's oldest independent bookshops, now on D'Olier Street. Strong on Irish writing, politics, and literature — with a fine café upstairs for when you need to sit down and start reading immediately.
availabilityNote: Café upstairs — great for settling in with a new purchase

title: Chapters Bookshop
description: Dublin's best second-hand bookshop on Parnell Street — a genuine city institution. Huge range of pre-loved and new titles, and one of the few places left where a happy accident of browsing can completely change what you read next.

title: Hodges Figgis
description: Dublin's grandest bookshop on Dawson Street — four floors of books in a beautiful old building, with an excellent Irish section and the kind of browsable depth that's rare these days. Mentioned in Ulysses, which feels appropriate.
availabilityNote: Four floors — allow more time than you think

title: Temple Bar Book Market
description: An open-air second-hand book market in Barnardo Square every Saturday from 10:30am. Browsing a table of old paperbacks in the cobblestoned heart of the city is one of Dublin's simple pleasures — and you'll nearly always find something worth buying.
